newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says Franco-German military ties to go on.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says Franco-German military ties to go on.

text.p: France's President Jacques Chirac told visiting German President Roman Herzog on Wednesday he believed military cooperation between the countries would increase despite budget constraints.

"Our cooperation in the field of defence will continue and will develop despite the budgetary constraints imposed on both of us," Chirac said at a banquet for the German leader who was on the first day of a four-day state visit.
Chirac said examples of such cooperation were the Eurocorps army unit dominated by France and Germany "and such grandiose projects of the future as the Helios II and Horus satellites."

The Helios II spy satellite is a touchy issue since German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe recently said he could not afford Bonn's share of the project from his 1997 budget which was cut from initially planned levels as part of an austerity programme.
Chirac also said "a reunified European Germany has a first rank role to play in the security of our continent and the world."

Herzog said in his reply: "We French and Germans want together to build a strong European Union through the intergovernmental conference, with institutions and decision-making mechanisms that enable it to remain able to take action when the number of members grows.

"We are ready to open our Union to the young democracies of central and eastern Europe. France stands to benefit just as much from stability in the east as Germany does from stability in the south," Herzog said.
The German president's role is largely ceremonial, while Chancellor Helmut Kohl regularly coordinates policies with Chirac to foster closer integration within the European Union.

This first state visit by a German leader to France since 1984 was timed, however, to underline the closeness of ties a few weeks before Paris and Bonn are to launch a joint proposal for reform of EU institutions to make it more effective in police, justice, foreign and defence policy.
Kohl and Chirac plan a Franco-German initiative before an EU summit in Dublin in mid-December, officials said.
Dividing his time between Paris and Bordeaux, where Prime Minister Alain Juppe is mayor, Herzog plans to stimulate a Franco-German intellectual discussion on civil rights issues.
While in Paris, Herzog is to speak at a conference on the influence of the values of the 1789 French Revolution on German unification and open an exhibition about Berlin.
He will also meet political leaders and heads of the Jewish community leaders as well as visit Paris' main Synagogue.
Herzog, a Bavarian Christian Democrat and former chief justice of Germany's Federal Constitutional Court, has been president since 1994.
